title: Binary data & typed arrays
lede: Raw byte buffers and the typed views over them, the layer every networking, crypto, and file-I/O path is built on. The recurring divergence is construction: a TypedArray can only be built in a variable declaration's initializer, never as a general expression, and none carry a `.buffer` back-reference (ArrayBuffer, Blob, and Node Buffer are the exceptions — they're general expressions). ArrayBuffer, DataView, SharedArrayBuffer, Atomics, and a real bigint-backed BigInt64Array/DataView 64-bit path are all here, so binary layouts round-trip byte-exactly; the text-shaped readers (Blob.text, Buffer.toString) still truncate at an embedded null byte.

entries.name: ArrayBuffer
entries.description: A fixed-length, zero-initialized (calloc'd) raw byte buffer, with .byteLength and .slice(start?, end?) (a copy, with array-slice negative-index/clamping rules). Unlike the TypedArrays below, it's a general expression — it works anywhere, not just in a variable declaration's initializer.

params.name: byteLength
params.desc: Size of the buffer in bytes.

entries.name: Uint8Array / Int8Array / Uint16Array / Int16Array / Uint32Array / Int32Array / Float32Array / Float64Array
entries.statusRow: Uint8Array / Int8Array / Uint16Array / Int16Array / Uint32Array / Int32Array / Float32Array / Float64Array
entries.description: Typed views over bytes, in three construction forms: a size (own new zero-filled buffer), an existing ArrayBuffer (a view sharing the same memory — writes through one view are visible through any other view over the same buffer, including a differently-typed one), the sub-range form new XArray(buf, byteOffset, length?), or a number[]/array literal/another TypedArray (a copy). Indexing, .length, the whole number[] HOF/iterator surface, plus the TypedArray-specific .set(source, offset?), .subarray(start?, end?) (a view, not a copy), and .byteLength. Non-clamped writes wrap mod 2^width, matching real JS.

returns.desc: A typed view or an own buffer.

differences: Construction is restricted to a variable declaration's initializer — `new Uint8Array(...)` can't appear as a general expression (TypedArrays weren't in scope for the change that lifted the identical restriction on plain array literals and `new Array<T>(...)`/`new Map<K,V>()`/`new Set<T>()`/`new EventEmitter<T>()`, but not for TypedArrays)

No `.buffer` property (would require every TypedArray, including the "own buffer" form, to carry a back-reference to a real `ArrayBuffer` object — a shape change from the plain `{ptr,i64}` array representation)

entries.name: BigInt64Array / BigUint64Array
entries.description: 64-bit typed arrays whose elements are stored as raw i64/u64 but cross the language boundary as real arbitrary-precision bigint handles — writes require a bigint (a plain number is the spec's TypeError), reads wrap losslessly, so values above 2^53 round-trip exactly. Atomics load/store/RMW/compareExchange work on them, lowered to the same seq_cst i64 atomics.
differences: The vardecl-only construction restriction and missing `.buffer` above apply here too

Only an explicit method allow-list is supported — indexing r/w, `.length`/`.byteLength`, `.at`, `.set`, `.subarray`, `.slice`, `.fill`, `.reverse`, for-of, `Atomics.*`; everything else (`.map`/`.filter`/`.reduce`/`.indexOf`/`.sort`/`.join`/iterator objects/…) is a compile-time rejection, never a raw-scalar leak
Compound element assignment (`a[0] += 1n`) is rejected — load, compute, assign
`console.log` of a *whole* array prints raw element values without the `n` suffix (single-element reads print correctly)
`Atomics.wait`/`notify` stay `Int32Array`-only

entries.name: Uint8ClampedArray
entries.description: A Uint8Array whose write path uses the spec's ToUint8Clamp instead of wrapping — values clamp to [0,255], floats round half to even (254.5 → 254, 255.5 → 255), and NaN → 0, on every write (element assignment including compound, construction, .set, .fill, and .map's result store). Reads are plain u8, so the entire read-side method surface works unchanged.
entries.snippet:
const clamped = new Uint8ClampedArray([-1, 300, 254.5, 255.5])
console.log(clamped[0], clamped[1], clamped[2], clamped[3]) // 0 255 254 255
differences: The vardecl-only construction restriction and missing `.buffer` above apply here too

entries.name: DataView
entries.description: Endian-controlled binary access over an ArrayBuffer: full get/set × Int8..Uint32/Float32/Float64 and BigInt64/BigUint64 (real bigint values, unsigned above 2^63 correct) with the spec's per-call littleEndian flag (default big-endian, via llvm.bswap), plus .byteLength/.byteOffset/.buffer (an aliasing-identical ArrayBuffer). RangeError on out-of-bounds access and construction.
differences: No `getFloat16`

entries.name: Blob
entries.description: An immutable binary value with a MIME type, built from mixed string/TypedArray/ArrayBuffer/Blob parts — a general expression. Exposes .size/.type, .slice(start?, end?, contentType?) (a copy; type never inherited, per spec), awaitable .text()/.arrayBuffer()/.bytes() returning copies, and .stream() → ReadableStream<Uint8Array>.
differences: `.stream()` delivers the whole blob as one `Uint8Array` chunk, not incrementally
The parts argument must be an inline array literal; no `endings` option; the `type` string is stored as-is (no spec lowercasing)
`.text()` truncates at an embedded null byte (the standard string-boundary caveat)

entries.name: SharedArrayBuffer
entries.description: Identical representation to ArrayBuffer (all view constructions, .byteLength, .slice() — which returns a new SharedArrayBuffer, per spec — and DataView work unchanged), but postMessage/workerData/structuredClone share it by reference instead of deep-copying, the spec's semantics. The backing memory for cross-thread Atomics.
differences: No `growable`/`grow()`
Crosses a worker boundary whole or as an object field; a TypedArray **view** doesn't cross — send the buffer, re-view on the other side
Views over it can't be captured by closures (the general array-capture limitation), so cross-thread handlers re-view inside the handler

entries.name: Atomics
entries.description: load/store/add/sub/and/or/xor/exchange/compareExchange on any integer TypedArray including BigInt64Array/BigUint64Array (bigint operands/results), lowered directly to seq_cst LLVM atomics; float TypedArrays are a compile-time rejection. wait(ta, i, expected, timeoutMs?) returns "ok"/"not-equal"/"timed-out"; notify(ta, i, count?) returns the wake count — a portable futex substitute. Atomics.isLockFree(n) is true for 1/2/4/8.
differences: `wait` blocks the whole calling thread (event loop and fibers included) — allowed on the main thread (Node posture); no `waitAsync`
`wait`/`notify` are `Int32Array`-only (spec minus the BigInt64 half)
Index is bounds-unchecked, matching ordinary TypedArray indexing

entries.name: Node Buffer (Buffer.from/.alloc/.toString(encoding)/.write/etc.)
entries.description: A Buffer IS a Uint8Array — indexing, .length, .slice/.subarray, numeric .fill/.indexOf/.includes, HOFs, for-of, .set, .byteLength, and fs.writeFileSync(buffer) all share the TypedArray machinery; Buffer.from(...)/.alloc(...) are general expressions (call syntax, no vardecl restriction). Codecs both directions — utf8, hex, base64, base64url, latin1/binary/ascii — plus full read/write{U}Int{8,16,32}{LE,BE} + Float/Double + BigInt64/BigUInt64 accessors with catchable RangeError bounds checks.
entries.snippet:
const hello = Buffer.from("Hello");            // utf8 bytes
console.log(Buffer.from("4869", "hex").toString())      // Hi
console.log(hello.toString("base64"))          // SGVsbG8=
const pkt = Buffer.alloc(12)
pkt.writeBigInt64BE(9007199254740993n, 4)
differences: No `utf16le`/`ucs2` encodings (the compiler's strings are UTF-8-native)
Encoding arguments must be compile-time string literals
`Buffer.from(arrayBuffer)` **copies** (Node views); `Buffer.concat`'s list must be an inline array literal

String-valued `.fill`/`.indexOf`/`.includes`/`.lastIndexOf` unsupported (number forms work); no 4-arg `.write(string, offset, length, encoding)` form; no `.swap16/32/64`, `.toJSON`, `Buffer.of`, `Buffer.isAscii`/`Buffer.isUtf8`, arbitrary-width `readIntLE(offset, byteLength)`, `poolSize`/`allocUnsafeSlow`
`.toString()` (utf8/latin1) truncates at an embedded null byte
